title: Generate All Feature Combinations
real_world_story: An AI configuration system has a set of optional features that can be enabled or disabled independently. The system needs to determine every possible feature configuration that can be created.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Power Set generation where every feature can either be selected or excluded

problem_statement: Given N distinct feature IDs, generate all possible subsets of these features. Each feature can either be included or excluded from a configuration. Print the total number of possible configurations.
task: Determine the number of possible feature configurations that can be generated from the given features.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated distinct feature IDs.
output_format: Print the total number of possible feature configurations.

examples.explanation: Each of the three features can either be selected or excluded, giving 2^3 = 8 configurations.
Four independent features produce 2^4 = 16 possible configurations.

expected_algorithm.name: Power Set
expected_algorithm.reason: Each feature has two possible states, selected or not selected, so N features produce 2^N possible configurations.

hint: Each feature has two possible states.
The number of configurations doubles whenever another feature is added.
Use the relationship between a set and its power set.
For N features, the number of configurations is 2^N.
real_world_takeaway: Power-set reasoning helps configuration systems understand how many possible combinations can be generated from a set of optional features.
